findings.problem: New privacy 'Subprocessors' section names Stripe as an active payment subprocessor ('Stripe processes payments (test mode at this stage).' / ua.ts:340), but Stripe has ZERO code presence in the repo. The only payments provider is the in-repo emulator (src/shared/config/env.ts: PaymentsProviderName = 'emulator', hard-disabled in production). Disclosing a subprocessor data-flow that does not exist is an inaccurate legal statement in a change whose sole purpose is privacy accuracy. (Precedent: the offer doc line en.ts:402 pre-dates this diff, so the inaccuracy already existed there, but this diff newly asserts it in the GDPR privacy policy.)
findings.fix: Either mark the Stripe line as a planned/TODO placeholder like the other unresolved legal facts ('[TODO: pending payment-provider integration]'), or describe the actual current mechanism (payments emulator, no live processor), so the subprocessor disclosure matches the code.

findings.problem: The 'Your rights' export line caveats only that 'Job-description text is not yet included', but the PDF export (src/app/api/account/export/account-export-pdf.tsx) also omits the extracted requirements and the tailored results/bullets — it exports only jobTitle, matchScore, date, and status. The 'What we store' section lists all of those as stored, so a reader is under-informed about export completeness (portability gap wider than disclosed).
findings.fix: Broaden the caveat to note that requirements and tailored results are also not yet exported, or generalize to 'tailoring metadata only', keeping the 'being expanded' hedge.

findings.problem: Legal 'Plans' summary states 'Ultra: a higher-tier subscription with the flagship model and higher limits.' There is no per-plan model routing or per-plan limit differential in code — resolveLlmProvider() uses a single global getLlmModel(), and paid access (hasPaidAccess) is binary across pro/ultra/job_hunt_pass. Restates a pre-existing marketing claim (T2) onto a legal page without substantiation. Root cause is the pre-existing model-routing gap, outside this diff's scope.
findings.fix: Either implement per-plan model selection to back the 'flagship model' claim, or soften the legal-page wording to what is true today (e.g. 'a higher-priced tier'), or mark the flagship-model capability 'coming soon' consistent with the pricing card treatment.
